q1: SELECT O1.SEAT_ID FROM CINEMA O1 WHERE O1.FREE = 1 AND ((SELECT FREE FROM CINEMA O2 WHERE O2.SEAT_ID = O1.SEAT_ID - 1) = 1 OR (SELECT FREE FROM CINEMA O2 WHERE O2.SEAT_ID = O1.SEAT_ID + 1) = 1)
q2: SELECT DISTINCT C1.SEAT_ID FROM CINEMA C1 JOIN CINEMA C2 ON (C1.SEAT_ID=C2.SEAT_ID -1 OR C1.SEAT_ID=C2.SEAT_ID + 1 ) AND C2.FREE =1 AND C1.FREE =1

counterexample: INSERT INTO CINEMA (SEAT_ID, FREE) VALUES (1, false), (2, true), (3, false);
explanation: Q1 checks for seats that are free and have at least one adjacent seat that is also free, while Q2 looks for pairs of adjacent free seats.
counterexample_dsp: A cinema with three seats, where the middle seat is free and its two adjacent seats are occupied. Q1 should return the middle seat, while Q2 should not return any seat as it is looking for pairs of adjacent free seats.
